tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE vibration rose 2.1→4.6 mm/s over six weeks without plateau, still below alarm; loss of this unspared gas-export compressor would send the platform to recycle and cut production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist today: diagnose NDE vibration, set operating/repair disposition; correct per findings, trend daily and confirm post-repair vibration meets specialist-approved limits. Obtain source-required attention today. Review current spectra, status and limits.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: For continued gas-export compression, the six-week increase from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s with growing spectral components supports strong progression. Remaining below alarm limits the assessment: neither imminent loss nor an actual compression failure is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this single gas-export compression train would send the platform to recycle and cut production within an hour, with no spare or workaround. This supports severe operational consequences, not an invented extreme accident scenario.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first start, then started on attempt 2 after about 8 s cranking and made rated pressure; 22.8 V at rest raises starting-system doubt, risking firewater on demand, while FW-8101 later made 9.2 vs 11 barg with flow unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Responsible engineer to set operating/repair disposition; correct faults found. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test batteries, charger, start circuit/air. Verify FW-8101 pressure/flow capability. Prove first-attempt starts and rated pressure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is FW-8102 starting on demand to supply firewater. The first attempt failed during the June 3 weekly test. Attempt 2 succeeded after about eight seconds of cranking, followed by normal running at rated discharge pressure. This confirms an interrupted starting function, not continuous pump unavailability. The 22.8 V measurement was at rest and does not establish battery performance during cranking or prove the cause.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start delays or prevents this pump's firewater contribution during a fire, creating credible major-accident and personnel-injury exposure. FW-8101 is the designated alternative, but its later June 17 observation showed 9.2 barg against 11 barg design with flow unmeasured; full backup capability cannot be credited. This does not establish that FW-8101 failed or that total firewater capacity is insufficient. Both pumps being unavailable would require production shutdown.

tickets.summary: PL-1002 window 2 near the low-point drain has CUI wall loss to 6.2 mm versus 7.4 mm minimum, threatening full-wellhead-pressure hydrocarbon containment; adjacent windows are within tolerance.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to assess fitness and operating/repair disposition; repair wall loss and water ingress to approved plan; verify wall >=7.4 mm and containment. Extend UT; verify repairs and current state. Check personnel exposure and release controls.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pressure containment of the production flowline. Wet insulation, heavy scaling and 6.2 mm wall below the 7.4 mm minimum establish advanced degradation, supporting the upper advanced-damage band. Adjacent windows remain within tolerance. Neither imminent rupture nor actual containment loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of containment would release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure, creating credible major-accident and personnel-injury exposure. No redundant line is recorded. This supports severe consequence, but release magnitude, personnel exposure and effective mitigation are insufficiently defined to justify an extreme band.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is this detector head's hydrocarbon-gas detection response. No response to 50 percent LEL gas, repeated with a second cylinder, confirms head-level function loss regardless of the remaining voted capability.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this compression-module gas-detection channel moderately degrades protection rather than defeating the group: the other two heads responded correctly. The 2oo3 arrangement retains capability but loses tolerance to another head failure.

tickets.summary: CR-5001 hoist rope has 6 broken wires/lay versus 10 discard at the max-radius drum section, with poor lubrication; hook, sheaves and structure are satisfactory. Failure risks a dropped load and stopped offloads, disrupting logistics within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Lifting engineer/surveyor: inspect full rope, restore lubrication, direct renewal as needed; verify <10 breaks/lay and set lifting-standard reinspection. Confirm rope trend and repair status. Check lift loads and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is main-hoist load support during lifting. Six broken wires per lay versus a discard criterion of ten supports remaining margin, but poor lubrication warrants correction. No progression rate or operational function loss is established; this supports limited degradation rather than imminent failure.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the load-supporting hoist rope presents a credible dropped-load injury hazard. Crane unavailability would also prevent supply-boat offloads, creating logistics problems within days, with no redundant crane identified. Actual loads and personnel exposure remain unknown; extreme consequences are not established.

tickets.summary: Port freefall lifeboat LB-4102 is declared unavailable after notchy release operation above specified force; certification is withheld, reducing evacuation capacity. Remaining certified capacity versus POB is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect and overhaul release gear under class surveyor-approved disposition. Verify current POB against certified available evacuation capacity. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Verify availability and capability of LB-4101. Class-witness release test to spec; recertify.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is reliable, compliant release for launch of LB-4102. The survey demonstrated operation outside specification, certification was withheld and the craft was declared unavailable: required capability is already lost, irrespective of partner availability.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this craft's launch capability reduces installation evacuation capacity and creates credible major-accident personnel exposure. LB-4101 is only a registry redundancy claim; its capability is unverified. Neither a capacity deficit below POB nor total evacuation loss is established.

tickets.summary: PSV-3420's tag is illegible, but March 2025 certification remains valid and the valve appears sound; no impairment is evidenced, although loss of its compressor-discharge overpressure protection would be severe.
tickets.recommended_action: Replace the corroded tag using authorized certification details; verify legibility and retain the two-year pop-test cycle.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is compressor-discharge overpressure relief. In-date March 2025 recertification, satisfactory observed valve condition and the engineer's operational reassurance support little indication of near-term function loss. Label corrosion is not valve deterioration.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Hypothetical loss of compressor-discharge overpressure protection creates severe pressure-integrity and personnel-safety exposure. No redundant valve is listed. This supports the severe band, but the supplied scenario does not establish extreme consequences; the tag's minor repair scope does not reduce this impact.

tickets.summary: FW-8101 ran at 9.2 vs 11 barg design with flow unmeasured, casting doubt on firewater delivery despite first-time start; backup remains unverified after FW-8102's earlier failed first start, and dual unavailability requires shutdown.
tickets.recommended_action: Firewater engineer to disposition; inspect test valves/pump, repair as found; retain weekly tests. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Verify duty criteria; retest flow/11 barg. Verify FW-8102 start/delivery and repair status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pump A's required firewater delivery, not starting. Running pressure of 9.2 barg against 11 barg design is a meaningful performance precursor. First-time starting and normal engine parameters are confirmed, but unmeasured flow and missing duty acceptance criteria prevent confirmation of required-function loss. No progression is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of required firewater delivery creates a severe fire-protection consequence, including personnel exposure during a fire. Healthy backup cannot be credited: on 3 June FW-8102 failed its first start, started on its second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking, then ran normally and achieved rated discharge pressure; batteries measured 22.8 V at rest. Its restoration and current capability are unknown. This does not establish simultaneous unavailability or a current capacity shortfall. Both pumps unavailable would require production shutdown.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on K-3401’s second-stage discharge line threatens to become a dropped object and injure personnel; the finding explicitly identifies no process concern.
tickets.recommended_action: Control the drop zone; inspect cladding and adjacent fixings; secure or replace under maintenance engineer disposition and verify secure retention. Check drop height, mass and personnel access.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is retention of the discharge-line cladding, not gas compression. Loose cladding already flapping in wind supports advanced degradation and likely progression toward detachment, although complete detachment is not confirmed. The earlier June 2 bearing-vibration observation is a separate mechanism and does not establish causation or progression of the June 19 cladding defect.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of cladding retention creates a credible dropped-object injury hazard, supporting a material consequence rather than a housekeeping-only assessment. Height, mass and personnel exposure are unknown, so severe or extreme injury consequences are not asserted. The explicit absence of process concern excludes transferring the compressor-trip production consequence to this failure path.
